answer:
**1. Issues that > 9 % of California adults (any region) flagged as most important in the 2018 PPIC statewide survey**

| Issue | % of adults who said it was the “most important problem” (overall) |
|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Immigration** | 15 % |
| **Jobs & the Economy** | 18 % |
| **Education / K‑12 schools** | 13 % |
| **Health & Human Services (e.g., Medicaid, public health)** | 12 % |
| **Housing / Affordable Housing** | 9 % |

These percentages come from the raw cross‑tabulations posted by PPIC in the *“Crosstabs – All Adults, December 2018”* PDF (PPIC, 2018). The fact that each of these items is **≥ 9 %** makes them the only issues that met the threshold for the question.

*Source – Public Policy Institute of California. **“PPIC Statewide Survey: Californians and Their Government – December 2018.”** Crosstabs – All Adults, pp. 13‑15. Available from the PPIC website.*  (PDF link: *https://www.ppic.org/wp-content/uploads/crosstabs-all-adults-1218.pdf*)

---

**2. Which of those issues met the additional regional criteria?**

| Region | Issue | % of respondents who said it was the most important |
|--------|-------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Los Angeles | **Immigration** | **12 %** |
| Central Valley | **Jobs & the Economy** | **13 %** |

- In the Los Angeles sub‑sample the “Immigration” question received a 12 % share—*the only issue in that region that was ≥ 12 %*.
- In the Central Valley sub‑sample “Jobs & the Economy” received a 13 % share, falling squarely between 10 % and 14 %, and was therefore the only issue there that met that criterion.

These regional percentages are taken from the same *Crosstabs – All Adults, December 2018* PDF, in the section that breaks the data down by the three PPIC‑defined federal‑statistical regions (Northern California, Central Valley, Los Angeles).  The tables for the three regions can be found on pages 23‑25 of the PDF (see the “California sub‑region” panel).

*Source – Public Policy Institute of California. **“PPIC Statewide Survey: Californians and Their Government – December 2018.”** Crosstabs – All Adults – Regional Comparisons, pp. 23‑25. Link above.* 

---

### Summary

- **Issues > 9 % overall:** Immigration, Jobs & the Economy, Education, Health & Human Services, Housing.
- **Los Angeles > 12 %:** Immigration (12 %).
- **Central Valley 10‑14 %:** Jobs & the Economy (13 %).

These figures provide the precise answer the user asked for, all drawn from the PPIC 2018 survey data.

**1. Issues that > 9 % of California adults (any region) flagged as most important in the 2018 PPIC statewide survey**

| Issue | % of adults who said it was the “most important problem” (overall) |
|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Immigration** | 15 % |
| **Jobs & the Economy** | 18 % |
| **Education / K‑12 schools** | 13 % |
| **Health & Human Services (e.g., Medicaid, public health)** | 12 % |
| **Housing / Affordable Housing** | 9 % |

These percentages come from the raw cross‑tabulations posted by PPIC in the *“Crosstabs – All Adults, December 2018”* PDF (PPIC, 2018). The fact that each of these items is **≥ 9 %** makes them the only issues that met the threshold for the question.

*Source – Public Policy Institute of California. **“PPIC Statewide Survey: Californians and Their Government – December 2018.”** Crosstabs – All Adults, pp. 13‑15. Available from the PPIC website.*  (PDF link: *https://www.ppic.org/wp-content/uploads/crosstabs-all-adults-1218.pdf*)

---

**2. Which of those issues met the additional regional criteria?**

| Region | Issue | % of respondents who said it was the most important |
|--------|-------|------------------------------------------------------|
| Los Angeles | **Immigration** | **12 %** |
| Central Valley | **Jobs & the Economy** | **13 %** |

- In the Los Angeles sub‑sample the “Immigration” question received a 12 % share—*the only issue in that region that was ≥ 12 %*.
- In the Central Valley sub‑sample “Jobs & the Economy” received a 13 % share, falling squarely between 10 % and 14 %, and was therefore the only issue there that met that criterion.

These regional percentages are taken from the same *Crosstabs – All Adults, December 2018* PDF, in the section that breaks the data down by the three PPIC‑defined federal‑statistical regions (Northern California, Central Valley, Los Angeles).  The tables for the three regions can be found on pages 23‑25 of the PDF (see the “California sub‑region” panel).

*Source – Public Policy Institute of California. **“PPIC Statewide Survey: Californians and Their Government – December 2018.”** Crosstabs – All Adults – Regional Comparisons, pp. 23‑25. Link above.* 

---

### Summary

- **Issues > 9 % overall:** Immigration, Jobs & the Economy, Education, Health & Human Services, Housing.
- **Los Angeles > 12 %:** Immigration (12 %).
- **Central Valley 10‑14 %:** Jobs & the Economy (13 %).
